feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital leadership CV with clear positioning, relevant scope, and credible public-sector experience. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense, slightly repetitive across skills sections, and could sharpen impact by adding more outcomes and tightening formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership brand: the headline, summary, and experience consistently position you as a digital platform and communications leader.  
- Strong credibility: NACo progression shows advancement, ownership, and scale; metrics like 10,000+ pages and 3.5 million annual page views add weight.  
- Broad, modern capability set: web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia, and AI-enabled search create a compelling, current profile.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more quantified business/user impact would strengthen impact (e.g., engagement gains, efficiency improvements, adoption rates).  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual unless intentional branding; punctuation varies in lists; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—consider “A2 (learning).” No major misspellings or grammar errors otherwise.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and a few concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and de-duplicate: remove broad lists like “platforms, governance models and content operations” and avoid repeating competencies already listed elsewhere.
- Add scale and context from recent roles, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Use a more direct opening tied to target roles: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years…”
- Possible rewrite: Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector web ecosystems for high-volume, mission-driven organizations. Combines digital strategy, Drupal-based platform delivery, governance, analytics, and editorial operations to improve usability, publishing efficiency, and audience reach at enterprise scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- “Enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production” largely duplicates the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized distinctive leadership-level capabilities and used more concise, parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics and reporting systems • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Consider replacing “operations” with “leadership” where appropriate to better match seniority.
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” is slightly vague; “content discovery” is clearer and more specific.
- Use “web” instead of “website” for a more standard competency label.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider making Core Competencies shorter or more executive-level.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills’ “Public-sector and advocacy messaging.”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like an extension of the experience section and repeats themes already covered elsewhere. Tightening the wording and emphasizing distinct outcomes, formats, or technical scope will make the footer feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a brief lead-in like “Selected Recent Projects” and keep all entries in parallel past-tense structure.
- Tighten phrasing: “hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat” is clearer and more scannable.
- Make each project more distinct by highlighting what is unique: Drupal 10 build, campaign storytelling, conference installation, recurring video program.
- Consider shortening “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for ongoing campaign expansion.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series overlap with current/future role bullets; keep the footer more portfolio-style than responsibility-based.
- “Editorial storytelling” and “production/distribution across website, email and social” echo existing communications experience language.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical range, but it reads broad and overlaps with your NACo entries. Tighten it around what is new/recent here: enterprise improvement, Drupal delivery, and the AI-enabled search initiative.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client value: “Lead digital strategy and web modernization for a U.S. national membership organization, improving campaign delivery, content operations, and enterprise web governance.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one sharper line: “Built cross-functional publishing workflows, governance standards, and analytics practices to support coordinated communications across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal work more outcome-oriented: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including microsite templates, modular content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Keep the AI work as a standout final bullet: “Spearheading an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance,” “workflows,” and “analytics” already appear heavily in the NACo roles—avoid repeating all three separately here.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a concrete business outcome.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It would be sharper if the opening were less list-like and if each bullet emphasized outcomes, team leadership, and transformation rather than channel ownership alone.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening with a tighter summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a national association.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen impact language on channels and analytics: add growth, engagement, efficiency, reporting cadence, or decision-making improvements if available.
- Combine governance/operations bullets for concision: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio and formalized publishing standards, governance, and cross-department planning to scale multimedia and digital operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video production/studio language may duplicate earlier NACo roles; emphasize building institutional capacity here, not recurring content production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned at this level versus broader team leadership later.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social, and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-oriented: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Recast workflow bullets with stronger verbs: “Built tighter editorial planning across communications, advocacy, and program teams, improving publishing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthened editorial planning/coordination” and “improved publishing workflows” are close; combine them into one stronger bullet.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strategically in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and outcomes-oriented capabilities rather than generic skill labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance, workflow design & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience strategy, content planning & message clarity
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “platform modernization,” since those are stronger and more evidenced in recent roles.
- If space allows, make one line more impact-linked, e.g. “Enterprise web strategy for high-volume, multi-publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” closely duplicates “Multi-channel communication” in Core Competencies.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. Use this topline item to emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than repeating software names.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Remove lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is required for target roles.
- Group platforms strategically: lead with Drupal/CMS modernization because that is most supported by recent experience; keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if central to target jobs.
- Prefer “content discovery” or “search strategy” over “experiences” for sharper phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform list in both sections.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies (“Workflow & systems architecture”).

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack that aligns with the most recent NACo leadership role, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it around business value and decision-making impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Digital analytics & optimization: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery.”
- Replace weaker items with outcome-oriented language: “KPI framework development,” “executive dashboarding,” “performance reporting,” and “search/SEO analysis.”
- Consider a tighter version: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery, KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance optimization.”
- If supported elsewhere, add scale or use context in a summary line instead of here (e.g. analytics supporting a 10,000+ page site and 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies; “executive reporting” is sharper.
- Avoid repeating too many platform names here if they are already emphasized in recent work bullets; keep this section concise.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong and relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list rather than a senior, impact-oriented capability statement. It should better reflect the recent studio-building and event-production leadership shown in your NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tasks/tools to higher-value capabilities: “Broadcast video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio buildout and operations,” “PTZ camera systems,” “Post-production editing.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • Studio operations and buildout • PTZ camera systems • Post-production editing”
- If space allows, make it more leadership-oriented: replace “Video production and editing” with “Video production leadership and editing.”
- Keep terminology consistent with recent experience; “broadcast-quality” and “in-house studio” are stronger cues than generic “virtual event production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia & live event production” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid/virtual event production” overlap with NACo bullets, so this skills line should stay concise rather than restating achievements.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s redundant with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” and doesn’t signal depth or recency. This section should either be tighter or add context that differentiates current, hands-on platforms from secondary familiarity.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent use: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider emphasizing depth: “Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, split by proficiency/relevance: “Primary: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint | Working knowledge: Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- Keep naming consistent with the CV’s impact language; avoid a bare list if you can add one qualifier tied to recent work.
- If this section must stay list-only, shorten to the most relevant 3–4 platforms and let older/less central tools drop.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the enterprise focus elsewhere unless supported by a project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize current, hands-on implementation tools and modernize the phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Replace with a tighter, more current list: HTML • CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used elsewhere consistently; they date the section without adding value.
- If space allows, add one short qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “for CMS customization, analytics deployment, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same stack in both places.
- jQuery may make the profile feel older unless it is still materially relevant in current freelance/Drupal work.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with stronger positioning already established in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from “tool list” to “automation + work management systems” and group by function for faster scanning.
- Prioritize tools tied to recent, higher-value work: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana; move chat tools lower or remove.
- Suggested rewrite: “Automation & Workflow Systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello; workflow automation, editorial planning, cross-team project tracking.”
- If accurate, add light outcome/context language elsewhere or in a summary line, e.g., “used to streamline publishing workflows and cross-department coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack and Teams function more as collaboration tools than workflow systems; consider moving them or dropping them for concision.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too thin to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use and align with the CV’s stronger recent email/communications leadership without repeating newsletter management already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (email campaign deployment, audience segmentation, journey setup, list management)”
- If accurate, prioritize the most recent/relevant platform first; e.g., put Dynamics 365 first only if it reflects current consulting work.
- Add one qualifier if true: “enterprise membership communications” or “association email operations” to better match the NACo/consulting context.
- Keep platform names concise and standardized; consider shortening to “Dynamics 365 CI/Journeys” if space is tight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “newsletters” or audience-size claims here; those are already covered in NACo experience.
- Don’t repeat analytics/reporting language already captured under Core Competencies and Analytics skills.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and misses a chance to sound more technical and outcome-oriented. In this section, tighten it into a cleaner capability stack rather than repeating broad terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • Google Tag Manager • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI reporting
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI reporting” or “Executive reporting” to sound more specific and business-facing.
- If accurate, add one higher-value implementation skill already implied by recent work, such as “analytics infrastructure” or “measurement strategy,” instead of a generic term.
- Keep the list ordered by technical depth/relevance: data collection → warehousing → reporting → optimization.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with Topline Skills [3]; consider trimming one of the two or making this version more tool-specific.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid overloading this section with the same framing.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete contributions and outcomes if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or process improvements.
- Tighten the management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “supervised/mentored a digital media associate” only if it was true people management.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this entry as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating governance/operations language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around concrete outputs so it complements, rather than repeats, the later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and outcomes: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities, translating findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to” with stronger verbs such as “produced,” “developed,” or “created.”
- If possible, add 1 measurable detail: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or types of multimedia assets delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content production; later roles already cover multimedia, video, and digital operations in more depth.
- Keep this entry focused on innovation/research support + first podcast launch, which is the clearest distinct contribution.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tighten it so it reads as a tools list, with only the most relevant production capabilities retained.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production • Podcast production”
- Standardize naming: use full Adobe product names for polish and consistency.
- Replace “Livestream studio workflows” with the cleaner, more outcome-oriented “Livestream production” unless you want to emphasize technical operations, in which case use “Studio and livestream operations.”
- If space is tight, consider dropping Illustrator unless it is actively used in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestream” and broader multimedia production already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; keep this entry tool-focused to avoid repetition.
- “Podcast production” ties to an older role, so keep it only if you want to preserve breadth rather than emphasize recent strengths.
